projects.name: Metatron
projects.what: A local image-to-3D forge. Feed it one reference photo, get back a textured mesh.
does: Runs Hunyuan3D locally on a single consumer GPU
Orchestrates its own VRAM so a 12GB card can host the forge and a language model without either dying
Job queue, live forge log, in-browser preview of the result
Exports textured GLB at up to 100k triangles

detail.intro: Image-to-3D generation usually means uploading your reference to somebody else's GPU and waiting. Metatron runs the whole pipeline on one machine — background removal, generation, texture painting — and gives it a control room: a queue you can watch, a log that says what stage it is at, and a viewer to orbit the result before you keep it.

sections.h: The hard part was memory, not modelling
sections.p: A 12GB card cannot hold a 3D generation model and a language model at once. Metatron treats VRAM as a resource to be scheduled rather than hoped for: the engine can be pinned hot for a run of jobs, or released so the assistant can have the card back. When a forge dies mid-run the service notices on restart and marks the job failed instead of leaving it hanging forever.
Every forge reports elapsed time and current stage — removing background, generating, texturing — so a seven-minute job is legible rather than a spinner. Failures name what died and when.
bullets: Queue with retry and discard per job
Output straight to GLB, ready for Blender

projects.name: Cloe
projects.what: A local AI companion with persistent graph memory, an autonomous mind, and a transparent desktop presence.
does: Graph memory of roughly 3,200 nodes and 29,000 connections across five typed trees
Confidence scoring with temporal decay, and a self-pruning compressor that protects core identity nodes
A per-pixel-transparent Tauri v2 orb that stays click-through where it is transparent
Researches on its own while idle — mood-driven behaviour that does not wait to be spoken to

detail.intro: Cloe is not a chat window with a personality prompt on top. She is a stack: a Flask backend, three local models, a memory that is a graph rather than a transcript, and a desktop orb with real per-pixel transparency. Everything runs on one consumer GPU. Nothing is sent anywhere.

sections.h: Memory is a graph, and it forgets on purpose
sections.p: Roughly 3,200 nodes and 29,000 connections across five typed trees — knowledge, mood, personality, relationship, desire. Every node carries a confidence score that decays over time, so something reinforced once in April does not carry the same weight as something reinforced weekly.
bullets: Five typed trees rather than one flat store
A compressor scores nodes on several factors and prunes with Jaccard similarity matching
Core identity nodes are protected from pruning — she cannot compress away who she is

sections.h: Three models, each doing what it is good at
sections.p: Mistral-Nemo 12B for conversation, qwen2.5-coder for a separate coding workspace, moondream for vision — all hosted by a local Ollama instance and coordinated through one Flask backend. An image is described by the vision model first, then reacted to in character by the conversational one; what is in the picture and what she thinks about it stay separate jobs.
Built with Tauri v2, using per-pixel transparency and coordinate mapping so clicks pass through the transparent regions to whatever is behind. She sits on the desktop rather than in a window.

sections.h: She acts when nobody is talking to her
sections.p: Self-directed research during idle periods, mood-driven responses that are not replies to anything, a diary on a schedule, and a wake-word listener. There is also a Minecraft mod bridge that lets her participate in a game and make her own decisions in it.
bullets: Minecraft mod bridge with independent decision-making
Raphael — a separate diagnostic service that watches logs for patterns

projects.name: Mytheder
projects.what: A Czech party card game, rebuilt from an abandoned repo and given a new identity for a Discord community.
does: Private rooms, five-character join codes, no accounts
1016 cards across five themed packs, loaded from JSON — no database
Chat, reconnect with backoff, rooms held open 90 seconds for dropped players
Whole theme is three colour tokens: re-skinning is a config change

detail.intro: The original author shut the project down and released the code. I rebuilt it: deleted the database, removed the dead accounts system, wrote the chat that was never finished, and re-skinned it for a Discord server that wanted its own version. It now runs as part of this site rather than on somebody's spare subdomain.

sections.p: The game only ever read cards from MySQL — three queries, no writes. All 1016 cards now load from JSON at boot and the entire database layer is gone. Adding cards is editing a file; there are no migrations.

sections.h: Most of the work was failure handling
sections.p: The bugs that actually ruined games were never about rules.
bullets: A one-second auth timeout was fine on localhost and killed every real connection through a proxy
One dropped socket ended everyone's game, because rooms were destroyed the moment they fell below three players
A small pack could run its prompt pile dry and take the room down with it
A player who dropped out of a full game was locked out by a headcount they were still part of

sections.p: The first build hard-coded one accent colour across ten components. Every colour now resolves from three tokens, so giving a new community its own version is a config change and four images rather than a hunt through the codebase.

projects.name: Monkey Paw
projects.what: One player makes a wish. Everyone else writes the catch that makes them regret it.
does: Free text instead of a deck — nothing ever runs out
A monkey's paw curls one finger per wish spent
Czech or English, chosen per room
Built on everything the card game taught me

detail.intro: A party game with no cards. The chooser writes a wish; everyone else writes the twist that ruins it; the chooser picks the one that hurt most. Because the content is typed rather than dealt, it never repeats and never runs out.

sections.h: Free text changes the failure modes
sections.p: A card game can always play a random card for someone who has gone quiet. You cannot autogenerate a person's joke — so a timed-out player gets a funny stock line instead of an empty slot, and three consecutive misses flips their paw over until they come back.

sections.h: The paw is the clock, then it isn't
sections.p: Each player's paw closes a finger per wish they spend. Round count is fixed when the game starts, so somebody who wanders off ends with fingers still up — a visible record of having been away — rather than holding the game open forever.
